To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the transition from biomass to clean fuels in Mexico is a complex process with trade-offs between different strategies.

the transition to clean fuels and cookstoves can deliver substantial mitigation in Mexico, and that the combination of a fast LPG penetration with CCS in high fNRB counties is the most effective option.

the combined dissemination of clean woodburning stoves in regions where there is nonrenewable fuelwood consumption and the dissemination of LPG in regions with high stacking, is the scenario that provides the greatest benefits for the mitigation of greenhouse gas emissions in Mexico.
In summary, our research is concerned with

a better understanding of the potential synergies and trade-offs between different clean cooking options and their spatial distribution in order to improve the effectiveness of public policy in the context of the Mexican residential sector.
the mitigation of GHG emissions in the residential sector of Mexico, which is the largest source of GHG emissions and black carbon in the country.
the development of integrated household energy strategies for rural areas, with a focus on the Mexican case.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a combined strategy of CCS and LPG, targeting counties with high fNRB, is the most cost-effective way of reducing emissions in Mexico.
a combination of CCS and LPG is the most effective strategy to achieve the highest GHG and BC emissions mitigation.

CCS-fNRB dissemination is an effective and efficient mitigation measure in Mexico and that the integration of CCS dissemination and LPG penetration in high fNRB counties is an effective strategy for GHG mitigation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the most effective scenario for GHG mitigation is a combined strategy of CCS plancha type stoves and LPG, which also has the advantage of being more socially equitable and less costly.

a combination of LPG and clean woodburners is a good option to mitigate GHG emissions in the residential sector, but it should be implemented in a strategic way to avoid stacking with open fires and to minimize the impact on the environment.

the combination of CCS and LPG in the Mexican rural residential sector is the most effective option for GHG mitigation and that the most effective strategy is the one that combines a high LPG penetration with a CCS plancha-type dissemination in counties with high fNRB.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combination of CCS dissemination in regions with high fNRB with LPG dissemination, can deliver the largest GHGs mitigation in the Mexican residential energy sector.
integrated energy transitions, combining CCS and clean fuels, may be the most cost-effective strategy for GHG mitigation in the residential sector.
the combination of CCS dissemination in high fNRB counties and LPG dissemination in low fNRB counties is the most effective way to mitigate GHG and black carbon emissions.
